simple.meaning: סַד (çad) is a Hebrew word meaning “the stocks.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: סַד (H5465) appears 2 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Job 13:27, with occurrences in Job.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to סַד (H5465) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in סַד (H5465) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: סַד (çad) / H5465 is traced through Job 13:27, Job 33:11 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

definitions.full: H5465. sad סַד noun [masculine] stocks , for confining feet of culprits (probably loan-word from Aramaic סַדָּנָא סַדָּא, ; Late Hebrew סַד , plural סַדִּין ); = Latin nervus , Greek ποδοκάκη ; — absolute בַּמּ רַגְלַיִם׳שִׂים Job 13:27 ( ᵐ5 κώλύμα ), 33:11 ( ᵑ6 ξύλό ); (compare synonym מַהְמֶּכֶת , and Greek equivalent there cited).
definitions.rootNote: from an unused root meaning to stop;

occurrences.englishText: You also put my feet in the stocks,
He puts my feet in the stocks.
